title: Multi-Cancer Early Screening with Non-contrast CT and Deep Learning.
summary: Alibaba DAMO's PANDA model exceeded mean radiologist sensitivity for pancreatic cancer on CT scans by 34.1% and found five cancers that the initial standard of care had missed.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In a retrospective test on 20,530 patients from July to October 2022, PANDA found five cancers that the initial standard of care had missed. One patient then had surgery with curative intent. A team of researchers from Chinese hospitals and Alibaba published the PANDA study, which reports this test, in Nature Medicine on 20 November 2023. Eight of its authors are Alibaba employees. The authors state that PANDA exceeded mean radiologist sensitivity by 34.1% and specificity by 6.3% for identifying pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. In its submission to the International Telecommunication Union, current as of June 2025, Alibaba DAMO reports a validation that involved 6,239 patients across ten centers and the cohort of 20,530 patients. No source reports a survival gain. In October 2026, surgeons in Brussels published a review in which they report that no study shows that the use of PANDA improves stage at diagnosis or survival.
purpose: Improve early cancer detection from non-contrast CT images.

ratings.reason: Cao and colleagues report that PANDA found five cancers that the initial standard of care had missed, and that one patient then had surgery with curative intent for a 1.5 cm pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
PANDA exceeded mean radiologist sensitivity by 34.1% and specificity by 6.3% for pancreatic cancer identification in the evaluated cohorts.
Lives saved and benefits from population screening are possible later effects. The authors of an independent 2026 review report that no study shows an effect on stage at diagnosis or survival.

ai_role.statement: In the reader study, 33 readers from 12 institutions and the model read the same 291 scans, so the comparison isolates what the model detects on its own. In the real-world test, clinicians confirmed the lesions that PANDA flagged, and the curative treatment followed their workup.

data.answer:
PANDA reports high pancreatic-lesion detection performance across large CT cohorts, including higher sensitivity and specificity than average radiologists.

Diagnostic metrics and 16 previously missed PDAC detections do not establish mortality reduction or net screening benefit. False-positive workup, overdiagnosis, stage shifts, and treatment outcomes require separate evaluation. The entry itself calls for randomized mortality trials, and a Breakthrough Device designation is not evidence of clinical efficacy.

The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.
